tagline: Operations consulting for companies that outgrew their spreadsheets

hero.title: The bottleneck isn't your team. It's the handoffs.
hero.body: We come in for twelve weeks, map how work actually moves through your business, and leave you with a process your people will use on a bad Monday.

services.title: Three ways we're usually brought in

items.name: Operations audit
items.body: Four weeks. We follow a real order end to end, interview the people who touch it, and hand back a map of where it stalls — with the three fixes worth doing first.

items.name: Systems implementation
items.body: You know which tool you need. We scope it, migrate the data nobody wants to touch, train the team, and stay on until it's the way work gets done rather than a second place to log it.

items.name: Fractional COO
items.body: Two days a week, on your leadership team. For the stretch between the founder running operations personally and being able to hire someone full-time to.

proof.quote: They found nine days of dead time in a fourteen-day process, and were straight about the fact that six of them were our own fault. The other three we fixed in a fortnight.
proof.name: Priya Raman

about.title: Small on purpose
about.body: Atlas is four people. That means the person who scoped your engagement is the person doing the work, and there is no layer of account management between you and an answer. It also means we take on eight clients a year, so we say no more than we say yes.
points: Fixed price, agreed before we start
A named lead on every engagement
Everything we build is yours, documented

contact.title: Tell us what's stuck
contact.body: A short note is plenty. We'll reply within a working day, and if we're not the right people we'll usually know someone who is.
